## Grille de densité (pour une famille ou un genre donné)

### Select by Taxon

```{r}

# # Select Familly
# unique(bota$Familly)
# Familly_focus = "Fabaceae"
# bota_focus <- bota[bota$Family == Familly_focus,]

# Select Genus
#unique(bota$Genus)
Genus_focus = "Eschweilera" # "Bagassa" "Eschweilera" "Eperua" "Pterocarpus" "Goupia" "Annona" "Ficus" "Garcinia" "Albizia" "Carapa" "Dicorynia" "Vouacapoua" "Qualea" "Inga" "Hevea" "Cecropia" "Anacardium"
bota_focus <- bota[bota$Genus == Genus_focus,]

```

### Grille de densité

```{r}
# Génération de la grille
i <- seq(1:30)
j <- seq(1:40)
grid <- expand.grid(i=i,j=j,presence=0) %>%
  mutate(
    x=5+10*(i-1),
    y=5+10*(j-1)
  )

# Fonction de comptage
count_R <- function(grid, bota, R) {
  # grid : position x et y des point de reférence
  # bota : position x et y des plantes
  # R : rayon d'interaction autour de la reférence
  
  # Remplir le vecteur de densité
  count <- purrr::map_int(seq_len(nrow(grid)), \(i)
  sum((grid$x[i]-bota$Xfield)^2 + (grid$y[i]-bota$Yfield)^2 <= R^2) # Théorème de pythagore
  )
  # retourner vecteur
  count
}

normalization <- function(count) {
  density <-  count / sum(count)
  density
}

# Différents périmètres de comptage
# 5m de rayon
grid$cinq <- count_R(grid, bota_focus, 5) %>% normalization()
# 10m de rayon
grid$dix <- count_R(grid, bota_focus, 10) %>% normalization()
# 15m de rayon
grid$quinze <- count_R(grid, bota_focus, 15) %>% normalization()
# 20m de rayon
grid$vingt <- count_R(grid, bota_focus, 20) %>% normalization()

```

### Plot plusieurs rayons

```{r}

library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

grid_long <- grid |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cinq, dix, quinze, vingt),
    names_to = "rayon",
    values_to = "count"
  )

grid_long$rayon <- factor(
  grid_long$rayon,
  levels = c("cinq", "dix", "quinze", "vingt"),
  labels = c("r = 5", "r = 10", "r = 15", "r = 20")
)

ggplot(grid_long, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = count)) +
  #geom_point(shape = 3, size = 0.5, col = "black") +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "black",
    high = "white"
  ) +
  coord_fixed() +
  facet_wrap(~ rayon, ncol = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(fill = "Densité de probabilité") 
```

## Traitement d'image

### Filtre Gaussien

```{r}
library(imager)

# 3-columns / matrice
mat <- matrix(grid$dix, nrow = 30, ncol = 40, byrow = FALSE) # exemple avec DIX

# matrice / image
img <- as.cimg(mat,x=30,y=40)

# Flou Gaussien
img_smooth <- isoblur(img, sigma = 2)

# Subplot
par(mfcol = c(1, 2))

# Plot 1
plot(img, xlim = c(0, 30), ylim = c(0, 40),
     xlab="x",ylab="y")

axis(1, at = c(0, 10, 20, 30), labels = c(0, 10, 20, 30))
axis(2, at = seq(0, 40, by = 10), labels = seq(0, 40, by = 10))


# Plot 2
plot(img_smooth, xlim = c(0, 30), ylim = c(0, 40),
     xlab="x",ylab="y")

axis(1, at = c(0, 10, 20, 30), labels = c(0, 10, 20, 30))
axis(2, at = seq(0, 40, by = 10), labels = seq(0, 40, by = 10))
legend(img_smooth)

```

### MCMC (Metropolis Hasting) sur image smooth

```{r}
set.seed(123)

# Matrice lissée
z <- as.matrix(img_smooth)

nx <- nrow(z)
ny <- ncol(z)

# coordonnées x et y réelles
x_vals <- seq(5, 5 + 10*(nx-1), length.out = nx)  # exemple correspondance i -> x
y_vals <- seq(5, 5 + 10*(ny-1), length.out = ny)  # exemple correspondance j -> y

# initial point (en indices)
i <- sample(1:nx, 1)
j <- sample(1:ny, 1)

# n° itérations
n_iter <- 10000
samples <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_iter, ncol = 2)

for(k in 1:n_iter){
  
  # propose new point (continu)
  i_new <- i + runif(1, -1, 1)  # déplacement continu
  j_new <- j + runif(1, -1, 1)
  
  # stay inside bounds
  i_new <- max(min(i_new, nx), 1)
  j_new <- max(min(j_new, ny), 1)
  
  # interpolation bilinéaire pour obtenir z continu
  i0 <- floor(i_new); i1 <- ceiling(i_new)
  j0 <- floor(j_new); j1 <- ceiling(j_new)
  di <- i_new - i0
  dj <- j_new - j0
  
  # handle edges
  i1 <- min(i1, nx)
  j1 <- min(j1, ny)
  
  # bilinear interpolation
  z_new <- (1-di)*(1-dj)*z[i0,j0] + di*(1-dj)*z[i0,j1] +
           (1-di)*dj*z[i1,j0] + di*dj*z[i1,j1]
  
  z_current <- z[i,j]
  
  # accept/reject
  alpha <- z_new / z_current
  if(runif(1) < alpha){
    i <- i_new
    j <- j_new
  }
  
  # stocker en coordonnées réelles
  samples[k, ] <- c(
    x_vals[1] + (i-1)*(x_vals[2]-x_vals[1]),
    y_vals[1] + (j-1)*(y_vals[2]-y_vals[1])
  )
}

samples <- as.data.frame(samples) %>%
  rename("x"="V1","y"="V2")

```

### K_means

```{r}
set.seed(123)  # pour reproductibilité

k <- 20  # nombre de clusters souhaité

# Appliquer K-means
kmeans_result <- kmeans(samples, centers = k, nstart = 25)  # nstart = nombre d'initialisations

# Ajouter les labels au dataframe
df_kmeans <- data.frame(
  x = samples[,1],
  y = samples[,2],
  cluster = factor(kmeans_result$cluster)
)

```

### Double plot

```{r}
library(gridExtra)

p1 <- ggplot(samples, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "red", size = 0.5) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "MCMC") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 400),
    breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100))

p2 <- ggplot(df_kmeans, aes(x = x, y = y, color = cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.5) +
  stat_density_2d(aes(fill = cluster, group = cluster),
                  color = "black", alpha = 0.1, geom = "polygon") +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  labs(title = "K-means clustering") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 400),
    breaks = seq(0, 400, by = 100))

grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```

### Problème :

On ne peux pas différencier par arbre, mais par cluster. Un même cluster peux contenir 1 gros arbre ou plusieurs petits. On fait l'hypothèse que la taille du cluster est proportionnelle à la Basal Area des arbres qui le compose.

## Analyse Interaction entre Plantes

```{r}
# Génération de la grille
i <- seq(1:30)
j <- seq(1:40)
grid <- expand.grid(i=i, j=j,
                            Bagassa=0,
                            Dicorynia=0) %>%
  mutate(
    x=5+10*(i-1),
    y=5+10*(j-1)
  )

# Select species
Specie_focus_1 <- c("Bagassa","guianensis")
bota_focus_1 <- bota[bota$Genus == Specie_focus_1[1] & bota$Species == Specie_focus_1[2],]
Specie_focus_2 <- c("Dicorynia","guianensis")
bota_focus_2 <- bota[bota$Genus == Specie_focus_2[1] & bota$Species == Specie_focus_2[2],]

# Passage en densité
# Bagassa
grid$BAG_vingt <- purrr::map_int(seq_len(nrow(grid)), \(i)
  sum((grid$x[i]-bota_focus_1$x)^2 + (grid$y[i]-bota_focus_1$y)^2 <= 20^2)
)
# Dicorynia
grid$DIC_vingt <- purrr::map_int(seq_len(nrow(grid)), \(i)
  sum((grid$x[i]-bota_focus_2$x)^2 + (grid$y[i]-bota_focus_2$y)^2 <= 20^2)
)

# Plot

p1 <- ggplot(grid, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  # espèce 1 (orange)
  geom_tile(aes(fill = BAG_vingt), alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "orange", limits = c(0, max(grid$BAG_vingt)))+
  geom_point(shape = 3, size = 0.5, col = "black") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(grid, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  # espèce 2 (bleu)
  geom_tile(aes(fill = DIC_vingt), alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue", limits = c(0, max(grid$DIC_vingt)))+
  geom_point(shape = 3, size = 0.5, col = "black") +
  theme_minimal()
 
grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)
```

```{r}

library(spatstat)

# Analyse intertype

# 1. Créer un objet ppp pour les deux types
xrange <- range(c(bota_focus_1$x, bota_focus_2$x))
yrange <- range(c(bota_focus_1$y, bota_focus_2$y))
window <- owin(xrange, yrange)

# Créer les points avec marquage
pp <- ppp(
  x = c(bota_focus_1$x, bota_focus_2$x),
  y = c(bota_focus_1$y, bota_focus_2$y),
  window = window,
  marks = factor(c(rep("type1", nrow(bota_focus_1)),
                   rep("type2", nrow(bota_focus_2))))
)

# 2. Calculer la fonction K-cross
Kc <- Kcross(pp, "type1", "type2")

# 3. Calculer la L-cross
Lc <- Lcross(pp, "type1", "type2")

# 4. Tracer
plot(Lc, main = "Analyse intertype Attraction/Répulsion")




```

```{r}
envelope_result <- envelope(
  pp,
  fun = Lcross,
  i = "type1",
  j = "type2",
  nsim = 99,       # nombre de simulations
  rank = 1,        # enveloppe 95%
  global = TRUE    # enveloppe globale
)

plot(envelope_result,
     main = "Analyse intertype avec enveloppes Monte Carlo",
     legendargs = list(x = "topleft", legend = c("Lcross", "Enveloppe 95% Monte Carlo")))

```

***Bagassa guianensis*** **et *Dicorynia guianensis* sont naturellement attirés**
